title: Config-delta replay harness and incident-driven regression safeguards
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary:
This ticket implements a reproducible "config-delta replay" harness and a small suite of automated regression tests that run whenever model or serving configuration changes are applied to staging/production. The goal is to close the evaluation gap exposed by recent incidents where config rollouts (quantization flags, KV cache TTL, batching policy) silently regressed output quality for a subset of prompts.
motivation: Recent incidents showed we lacked a fast, deterministic way to replay the exact request stream and config delta responsible for quality regressions. Postmortems pointed to missing pre-merge checks for config-level changes and insufficient coverage in eval suites for edge prompt clusters. This work reduces mean time to detect and revert quality regressions and prevents recurrence by gating config/model changes with automated checks.
acceptance_criteria: A1: A harness that can take a produced incident bundle (model version + config diff + sample request set) and replay it deterministically against a target runtime in <=30 minutes
A2: Automated regression tests that run as part of the config-change CI pipeline and return pass/fail within the deploy window (target: <45m), with failure creating a blocking deployment flag
A3: New eval metric "Delta-ROUGE-Quality" (prototype) is computed and surfaced in the regression alert payload and CI checks
A4: Dashboard tile and an incident runbook link are created for every failing regression so on-call can triage quickly
A5: Documentation and a short how-to for solutions/SEs on capturing incident bundles and creating replay jobs
approach: 1) Reuse incident bundle format from postmortem playbook and extend with precise config-delta encoding (per-field before/after). 2) Build a lightweight replay runner service that can mount the target model artifact and apply the delta in a sandboxed runtime (staging cluster). 3) Wire the runner to the eval harness to compute a small, focused set of metrics (quality, token divergence, hallucination flags) and compare against baseline thresholds. 4) Integrate runner with the config-change CI: PRs that touch model-serving flags trigger the harness; failing checks block merge. 5) Add an automated remediation flag that populates a rollback PR template and notifies the owner/team. 6) Create a cheap nightly job to run the harness against a sampled set of recent config changes to catch regressions that slipped through.
test_plan:
- Test vectors: start with incident sample sets from last 3 incidents (anonymized), expand to 500 prompts across prompt clusters.
- Matrix: run combinations of model variant (v1/v2), quantization (8-bit/4-bit), batching policy (conservative/aggressive), KV cache TTL (0/30s/300s).
- Metrics recorded: token-level perplexity delta, automated fidelity score, semantic-answer overlap (embedding cosine), and a yes/no hallucination hit rate.
- Thresholds: conservative defaults tuned to only surface meaningful regressions (configurable per-customer).
- CI integration: harness runs in ephemeral staging; if any metric crosses threshold, fail the pipeline and create an incident bundle artifact attached to the PR.
monitoring_and_alerts:
- Create a new Grafana dashboard 'Config Delta Replays' showing last 30 replays, top regressions, and regressions by config key.
- Register a Prometheus metric replay_regression_count and replay_latency_seconds.
- Add an Ops alert: if replay_regression_count >= 1 for a production config change, page on-call SRE and create a 'config-regression' incident channel.
- Post-failure hook generates a structured message with baseline/baseline-config diff links, failing prompts, and suggested rollback PR template.
rollout_plan:
Phase 1 (staging-only): deploy replay runner to staging for manual use by SRE/ML Eng; run replay on historical incidents.
Phase 2 (CI gating): enable runner as a required check for PRs that modify config flags or model pinning. Start with opt-in team 'runtime' + 'models'.
Phase 3 (enforced): expand required checks to all service teams and default thresholds.
Phase 4 (monitoring): nightly sampling run across recent prod config changes and integration with console alerts for customers using dedicated/private deployments.
risks_and_mitigations:
- Risk: False positives block deploys. Mitigation: conservative thresholds, allow manual override with documented exception flow and short-term 'soft-fail' period.
- Risk: Replay non-determinism due to runtime performance variance. Mitigation: sandbox using same model artifact and pinned runtime image; log seeds and RNG sources.
- Risk: Increased CI time. Mitigation: only run full matrix on PRs touching critical flags; otherwise run targeted subset and queue full matrix on merge to a staging release branch.
